Imagine riding a bike up a hill. Your friend asks how steep it is right now. You can't just say "I climbed 100 meters in 2 kilometers" because that's an average. They want the steepness at this exact spot. If you zoom in really close, the road looks like a straight line.

This "slope at one spot" is called the derivative. It's super important in machine learning, guiding us to reduce mistakes, just like finding the fastest way downhill. We'll learn to calculate it, use it to make curvy functions appear straight near a point, and extend this idea to many inputs.

To estimate square root 4.2 without a calculator, we use the known square root of 4, which is 2. The derivative of square root x at x equals 4 is one-fourth. Our estimate becomes 2 plus one-fourth times 0.2, giving us 2.05. This simple trick provides a very close answer.

For exams, always normalise direction vectors and evaluate partial derivatives at the specific point. Remember, differentiable means continuous, but not the reverse. The gradient points uphill fastest! Master the derivative as the slope, linear approximation, and the gradient's direction. Keep practicing, you've got this!
